title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
pacman::p_load(ggiraph, plotly, patchwork, DT, tidyverse,
               readxl, gganimate, gifski, gapminder)

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Importing Data

exam_data <- read_csv("../../data/Exam_data.csv")

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Interactive Dot Plot with Tooltip
ggiraph converts ggplot2 graphics into interactive SVG objects. We replace standard geoms with their _interactive counterparts and provide a tooltip aesthetic.

p <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
            aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_dotplot_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = ID),
    stackgroups = TRUE,
    binwidth = 1,
    method = "histodot") +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL)

girafe(ggobj = p,
       width_svg = 6,
       height_svg = 6 * 0.618)

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Hover Highlighting with data_id
data_id groups elements so hovering over one point highlights all points sharing the same value — useful for seeing class groupings at a glance.

p <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
            aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_dotplot_interactive(
    aes(data_id = CLASS),
    stackgroups = TRUE,
    binwidth = 1,
    method = "histodot") +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL)

girafe(ggobj = p,
       width_svg = 6,
       height_svg = 6 * 0.618)

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Combining Tooltip and Hover Effect

p <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
            aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_dotplot_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = CLASS,
        data_id = CLASS),
    stackgroups = TRUE,
    binwidth = 1,
    method = "histodot") +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL)

girafe(ggobj = p,
       width_svg = 6,
       height_svg = 6 * 0.618)

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Coordinated Multiple Views
Linking two plots so hovering over a point in one plot simultaneously highlights the same student in the other.

p1 <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
             aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_dotplot_interactive(
    aes(data_id = ID),
    stackgroups = TRUE,
    binwidth = 1,
    method = "histodot") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL)

p2 <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
             aes(x = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_dotplot_interactive(
    aes(data_id = ID),
    stackgroups = TRUE,
    binwidth = 1,
    method = "histodot") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL)

girafe(code = print(p1 + p2),
       width_svg = 6,
       height_svg = 3,
       options = list(
         opts_hover(css = "fill: #202020;"),
         opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.2;")
       ))

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Basic Interactive Scatter Plot
plot_ly() creates interactive web-based visualizations. Hovering reveals values; clicking the legend toggles groups.

plot_ly(data = exam_data,
        x = ~MATHS,
        y = ~ENGLISH,
        color = ~RACE)

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
ggplotly()
ggplotly() wraps any existing ggplot2 object to add interactivity with minimal extra code.

p <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
            aes(x = MATHS,
                y = ENGLISH,
                color = RACE)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggplotly(p)

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Coordinated Multiple Views with subplot()
Using highlight_key() and subplot() enables linked brushing — selecting points in one panel highlights the same records in the other.

d <- highlight_key(exam_data)

p1 <- ggplot(data = d,
             aes(x = MATHS,
                 y = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100),
                  ylim = c(0, 100))

p2 <- ggplot(data = d,
             aes(x = MATHS,
                 y = SCIENCE)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100),
                  ylim = c(0, 100))

subplot(ggplotly(p1),
        ggplotly(p2))

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Importing Population Data

col <- c("Country", "Continent")

globalPop <- read_xls("../../data/GlobalPopulation.xls",
                      sheet = "Data") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(col), as.factor)) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Static Bubble Plot
Before adding animation, we build the base ggplot2 bubble chart mapping Old (% aged) to x, Young (% young) to y, and Population to point size.

ggplot(globalPop,
       aes(x = Old,
           y = Young,
           size = Population,
           colour = Country)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 12)) +
  labs(title = "Global Population: % Aged vs % Young",
       x = "% Aged",
       y = "% Young")

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Animated Bubble Plot with gganimate
transition_time() animates the chart across the Year variable. The title {frame_time} updates automatically each frame.

ggplot(globalPop,
       aes(x = Old,
           y = Young,
           size = Population,
           colour = Country)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7,
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 12)) +
  labs(title = "Year: {frame_time}",
       x = "% Aged",
       y = "% Young") +
  transition_time(Year) +
  ease_aes("linear")

title: Hands-on Exercise 3: Interactive and Animated Data Visualisation with R
text:
Animated Bubble Plot with plotly
Using the frame aesthetic in plot_ly() adds a play button and year slider for interactive, user-controlled animation.

globalPop %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~Old,
          y = ~Young,
          size = ~Population,
          color = ~Continent,
          frame = ~Year,
          text = ~Country,
          hoverinfo = "text",
          type = "scatter",
          mode = "markers") %>%
  layout(showlegend = TRUE,
         xaxis = list(title = "% Aged",
                      zeroline = FALSE),
         yaxis = list(title = "% Young",
                      zeroline = FALSE))

title: Hands-on Exercise 2: Beyond ggplot2 Fundamentals
text:
Importing Data

exam_data <- read_csv("../../data/Exam_data.csv")

title: Hands-on Exercise 2: Beyond ggplot2 Fundamentals
text:
Beyond ggplot2 Annotation: ggrepel
Replacing geom_text() with geom_text_repel() to avoid overlapping labels.

ggplot(data = exam_data,
       aes(x = MATHS, y = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm,
              linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_label_repel(aes(label = ID),
                   fontface = "bold") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "English scores versus Maths scores for Primary 3")

title: Hands-on Exercise 2: Beyond ggplot2 Fundamentals
text:
Beyond ggplot2 Themes
Using theme_economist() from ggthemes.

ggplot(data = exam_data,
       aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20,
                 boundary = 100,
                 color = "grey25",
                 fill = "grey90") +
  theme_economist() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Maths Scores",
       x = "Maths Score",
       y = "Frequency")

title: Hands-on Exercise 2: Beyond ggplot2 Fundamentals
text:
Composite Plots with patchwork
Combining multiple plots into one figure.

p1 <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
             aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20,
                 boundary = 100,
                 color = "grey25",
                 fill = "grey90") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Maths Scores")

p2 <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
             aes(x = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20,
                 boundary = 100,
                 color = "grey25",
                 fill = "grey90") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of English Scores")

p3 <- ggplot(data = exam_data,
             aes(x = MATHS, y = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm,
              linewidth = 0.5) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100),
                  ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(title = "English vs Maths Scores")

(p1 / p2) | p3
